items.q: J. C. mentioned to me that between 1915 and 1918 he was running an elevator in New York City in the building where Bert Williams either lived or worked.

ctx.x: In the meantime I would like to share these thoughts that J. C. Johnson shared with me. One of the people that he mentioned was Lew Leslie's Blackbirds in 1932, and the time he referred to this is the beginning of musical comedy. Billy Butler, chairman of the J. C. Johnson Project's artistic committee and a very articulate and well educated man, three degrees from higher institutions, higher education, conducted the orchestra for the Blackbirds, and we know that he will be of great help to the Smithsonian in…

J. C. mentioned to me that between 1915 and 1918 he was running an elevator in New York City in the building where Bert Williams either lived or worked. He later mentioned that in the '20s Bert Williams lived at 134th and 7th Avenue. When I asked him what Harlem was like then, he said, 'It was the real Harlem back in the days of Billie Holiday and the Cha-Cha Club on 7th Avenue. It was a wide open village where people used to roam in perfect safety, people of all nationalities.'

He also indicated that Lenox Avenue was the last street to get rid of the trolley. He mentioned Langston Hughes and he and Langston writing something together. J. C. was disappointed about something in Langston and dropped the relationship. He did tell me that Langston initiated it. He still has the papers, the poem and the music in Wortsborough.
